create.note: workspace_id is not accepted from the client in personal runtime, and is required to match the active workspace runtime context otherwise — it is never taken as an arbitrary client override.

patch.desc: At least one field must be present in the request body — an empty PATCH is rejected.

behaviors.b1: A session belongs to exactly one owner (a user, optionally scoped to a workspace) — determined by the authenticated request context, not by client input.

message_behaviors.b1: A message can only be edited or deleted by the owner of the session it belongs to.
message_behaviors.b2: Undo restores the most recent recorded version and removes that history entry — it does not step further back than the last edit.
message_behaviors.b3: Editing or deleting a message does not currently adjust the session's cached message count field; it always reflects the live count instead.

errors.e400: Invalid request — including an empty PATCH body or no detected changes.
errors.e404: Session or message not found (or not owned by the caller).

research_discovery_page.eyebrow: Research & Discovery · Step 01 · How We Work
research_discovery_page.title: Understand Before You Build.
research_discovery_page.intro_p1: Every OpenQCore engagement begins with structured investigation. Before proposing artificial intelligence, automation, software or infrastructure, we study the problem as a system: its objectives, stakeholders, workflows, decisions, data, technologies, dependencies, constraints, risks and measurable outcomes.
research_discovery_page.intro_p2: Our discovery process combines research, systems thinking, engineering analysis and business reasoning to move from an observed challenge to a defensible problem definition.
research_discovery_page.intro_p3: Because the first question should not be:
research_discovery_page.intro_should_be: "What problem are we actually solving — what evidence supports it, what causes it, and what outcome needs to change?"
research_discovery_page.hero_tags: Research · Evidence · Systems Analysis · Business Analysis · Measurement
research_discovery_page.why_first_title: A Technology Is Not a Problem Definition.
research_discovery_page.why_first_p1: Artificial intelligence has become substantially easier to experiment with. Converting experimentation into measurable organizational value remains considerably harder.
research_discovery_page.stat_74_label: of companies had yet to demonstrate and scale tangible value from AI.
research_discovery_page.stat_74_source: BCG, Where's the Value in AI?, 2024 · n=1,000 senior executives.
research_discovery_page.why_first_p2: BCG's 2024 research, based on 1,000 CxOs and senior executives across more than 20 sectors and 59 countries, found that only 26% of companies had developed the capabilities needed to move beyond proofs of concept and generate tangible value from AI.
research_discovery_page.why_first_p3_insufficient: This does not mean that technology is ineffective. It means technology alone is insufficient.
research_discovery_page.why_first_p4: Organizations can begin with a model, platform or automation technology and only later discover that the underlying constraint lies elsewhere: fragmented processes, inaccessible data, unclear ownership, integration limitations, inadequate controls, poorly defined objectives or a problem that was never measured in the first place.
research_discovery_page.why_first_p5_consequence: OpenQCore therefore reverses the sequence: technology should be selected as a consequence of understanding the problem — not as a substitute for understanding it.
research_discovery_page.lenses_p1: Complex organizational problems rarely belong to a single discipline. OpenQCore investigates them through three complementary perspectives.

lens_scientific.title: Scientific Reasoning
lens_scientific.body: Scientific reasoning helps us distinguish observations from assumptions, formulate questions, examine competing explanations and determine what evidence would support or contradict a hypothesis. We do not assume that the first explanation is the correct one.

lens_systems.title: Systems & Engineering
lens_systems.tags: Systems · Interfaces · Data · Dependencies · Constraints · Reliability
lens_systems.body: Engineering analysis examines how components interact within the wider system — software, infrastructure, data, humans, processes, interfaces, external systems and operational dependencies.
lens_systems.iso_note: This perspective is consistent with modern systems-engineering thinking. ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 defines system lifecycle processes applicable to individual system elements and to systems-of-systems, with stakeholder involvement throughout the lifecycle.

lens_business.title: Business & Operations
lens_business.tags: Objectives · Economics · Processes · Risk · Value · Measurement
lens_business.body: Business analysis determines why the problem matters. We examine the desired outcome, affected stakeholders, operational impact, economic considerations, organizational constraints and how improvement would be measured.

research_discovery_page.system_bigger_title: The System Is Bigger Than the Model.
research_discovery_page.system_bigger_p1: AI transformation is often discussed primarily in terms of models and algorithms. The implementation evidence suggests a broader picture: BCG's 2024 research reported that approximately 70% of the challenges companies encountered in AI initiatives related to people and processes, approximately 20% to technology, and only 10% to algorithms.
research_discovery_page.stat_1020_70_source: BCG Build for the Future 2024 Global Study · n=1,000.
research_discovery_page.system_bigger_p2_framework_note: These percentages are BCG's research framework, not a universal law. But they reinforce an important engineering principle: the model is one component of a larger socio-technical system. For OpenQCore, discovery therefore examines not only the intelligence layer, but the operating environment into which that intelligence would be introduced.
research_discovery_page.methodology_title: From Observation to a Defined Problem.
research_discovery_page.methodology_p1: Discovery is conducted as a structured sequence of investigation. The exact depth varies with the engagement, but the analytical structure remains consistent.

stakeholder_objective_mapping.title: Stakeholder & Objective Mapping
stakeholder_objective_mapping.question: What outcome matters — and to whom?
stakeholder_objective_mapping.body: We begin by identifying the people, functions and systems affected by the problem. An organization's stated request is not automatically treated as the underlying objective — "we need an AI agent" describes a possible implementation, not yet the business or engineering problem.
stakeholder_objective_mapping.examines: Stakeholders · Decision Owners · Users · Business Objectives · Operational Objectives · Incentives · Dependencies · Conflicting Requirements

operational_workflow_analysis.title: Operational & Workflow Analysis
operational_workflow_analysis.question: How does the system actually operate today?
operational_workflow_analysis.body: We reconstruct the current operating process rather than relying exclusively on how that process is documented. Where appropriate, we establish quantitative baselines for the existing workflow.
operational_workflow_analysis.examines: Processes · Tasks · Decisions · Handoffs · Queues · Exceptions · Human Intervention · Bottlenecks · Rework · Information Flow

systems_data_audit.title: Systems & Data Audit
systems_data_audit.question: What technical environment are we working within?
systems_data_audit.body: We examine the architecture surrounding the problem, and investigate the data environment separately. This matters because an AI capability that works experimentally may still be unsuitable for production if the required information cannot be accessed reliably, securely or with sufficient quality.
systems_data_audit.examines: Applications · Services · APIs · Databases · Infrastructure · Integrations · Identity · Security · External Dependencies — and data availability, accessibility, structure, quality, lineage, ownership, coverage, freshness and sensitivity

market_contextual_analysis.title: Market & Contextual Analysis
market_contextual_analysis.question: What external environment shapes the problem?
market_contextual_analysis.body: A technically valid solution can still be operationally or commercially inappropriate. The scope depends on the engagement — a regulated healthcare system, financial platform and internal productivity tool do not require identical forms of contextual investigation.
market_contextual_analysis.examines: Market Conditions · Industry Structure · Regulation · Technical Standards · Competitive Environment · Technology Landscape · Customer Expectations · External Dependencies

constraint_risk_identification.title: Constraint & Risk Identification
constraint_risk_identification.question: What limits the solution space?
constraint_risk_identification.body: Constraints are treated as design inputs rather than surprises discovered during implementation. We also explicitly separate known facts, assumptions, known unknowns, dependencies and risks — because uncertainty should be documented, not silently converted into certainty.
constraint_risk_identification.examines: Technical, Operational, Budget and Time Constraints · Security, Privacy and Regulatory Requirements · Organizational Constraints · Adoption Risks · Integration Dependencies · Data Limitations

problem_definition_success_criteria.title: Problem Definition & Success Criteria
problem_definition_success_criteria.question: What exactly must change?
problem_definition_success_criteria.body: Discovery converges on a precise problem definition, covering the observed condition, evidence, root causes, affected system, baseline, target state, success criteria, constraints and explicit non-goals.
problem_definition_success_criteria.examines: Observed Condition · Evidence · Root Causes · Affected System · Baseline · Target State · Success Criteria · Constraints · Non-Goals

research_discovery_page.cycle_p1: Discovery is not simply a checklist completed once from left to right.
research_discovery_page.cycle_p3_interview: A stakeholder interview can reveal a previously hidden dependency.
research_discovery_page.cycle_p4_system: System analysis can change the problem definition.
research_discovery_page.cycle_p5_measurement: A measurement can contradict the original hypothesis.
research_discovery_page.cycle_p6_transition: Once sufficient confidence has been established: Validated Problem → Strategy & Architecture.
research_discovery_page.applying_p1: An observed problem and its underlying cause are not necessarily the same thing. Consider a simplified operational example.

observed_condition.label: Observed condition
observed_condition.body: Customer requests require 48 hours to process.

workflow_evidence.label: Workflow evidence
workflow_evidence.body: Requests move through multiple manual approvals.

system_evidence.label: System evidence
system_evidence.body: Relevant information exists across disconnected applications.

data_evidence.label: Data evidence
data_evidence.body: The same information is repeatedly retrieved and verified.

root_cause_hypothesis.label: Root-cause hypothesis
root_cause_hypothesis.body: Fragmented workflow and inaccessible information create repeated human work.

research_discovery_page.applying_p2_question_change: At this point, simply adding a conversational interface may improve the customer-facing experience without resolving the underlying processing constraint. The engineering question therefore changes from "How do we add AI?" to "Which intervention changes the causal mechanism producing the undesirable outcome?" — that distinction is central to Research & Discovery.
research_discovery_page.hypothesis_observation: Manual document verification is associated with a significant processing bottleneck.
research_discovery_page.hypothesis_hypothesis: A controlled document-intelligence workflow may reduce manual review while maintaining required verification controls.
research_discovery_page.hypothesis_evidence: Representative documents · Existing error rates · Exception patterns · Review requirements · Processing times
research_discovery_page.hypothesis_evaluation: Extraction quality · Exception rate · Human-review rate · Processing time · Failure modes
research_discovery_page.hypothesis_objective: The objective is not to prove that a proposed technology works. The objective is to determine whether the evidence justifies using it.
research_discovery_page.success_p1: If success is defined only after implementation, almost any result can be interpreted as success. OpenQCore therefore establishes relevant baselines and evaluation criteria during discovery.

cycle_time.title: Cycle Time
cycle_time.body: How long does the process take?

cost_per_operation.title: Cost per Operation
cost_per_operation.body: What resources does each transaction consume?

error_rate.title: Error Rate
error_rate.body: How frequently does the process produce an incorrect result?

throughput.title: Throughput
throughput.body: How much work can the system process?

human_effort.title: Human Effort
human_effort.body: How much manual intervention is required?

reliability.title: Reliability
reliability.body: How consistently does the system perform?

decision_quality.title: Decision Quality
decision_quality.body: How accurately or consistently are decisions made?

automation_rate.title: Automation Rate
automation_rate.body: Which operations can be completed without manual intervention?

risk_exposure.title: Risk Exposure
risk_exposure.body: What operational, security or compliance risk exists?

experience_metrics.title: Experience Metrics
experience_metrics.body: How does the process affect customers, employees or other users?

research_discovery_page.success_p2_structure: The structure is simple: Baseline → Intervention → Target → Measurement → Evaluation.
research_discovery_page.success_p3_cannot_evaluate: If the desired change cannot be described, the success of the solution cannot be meaningfully evaluated.
research_discovery_page.ai_risk_title: Capability Is Not the Same as Suitability.
research_discovery_page.ai_risk_p1: For AI-related engagements, discovery also examines whether the proposed use of AI is appropriate for the context in which it will operate. NIST's AI Risk Management Framework organizes AI risk-management activity around four functions, and specifically describes risk management as continuous across the AI lifecycle rather than a one-time compliance exercise.
research_discovery_page.ai_risk_p2_continuous: The framework also identifies characteristics associated with trustworthy AI, including validity and reliability, safety, security and resilience, accountability and transparency, explainability and interpretability, privacy enhancement, and management of harmful bias.
research_discovery_page.ai_risk_p3_proportionate: This does not mean every project requires the same governance architecture. Risk controls should be proportionate to the system, its context and the consequences of failure.
research_discovery_page.evidence_title: We Are Not Looking for Reasons to Use AI.
research_discovery_page.evidence_p1: We are looking for the intervention that the evidence supports. Recent evidence continues to reinforce the importance of redesigning work rather than simply placing AI on top of existing processes.
research_discovery_page.stat_two_thirds_label: of organizations had not yet begun scaling AI across the enterprise.
research_discovery_page.stat_39_label: reported AI-related EBIT impact at the enterprise level.
research_discovery_page.stat_mckinsey_source: McKinsey, The State of AI: Global Survey 2025.
research_discovery_page.evidence_p2_workflow: The same research identifies workflow redesign as a key characteristic of organizations obtaining greater value from AI — one reason OpenQCore investigates the operating model surrounding the technology rather than treating deployment itself as the objective.
research_discovery_page.evidence_p3_not_predetermined: OpenQCore does not begin discovery with a predetermined technical solution. The evidence may indicate that the appropriate intervention is process redesign, systems integration, conventional software engineering, data architecture, workflow automation, analytics, artificial intelligence, or a combination of them. In some cases, the evidence may indicate that building new technology is not justified at all.
research_discovery_page.evidence_p4_not_looking: OpenQCore does not recommend artificial intelligence because it is fashionable. We recommend it when the problem, evidence, economics and operating constraints justify its use — and we say clearly when they do not.
research_discovery_page.evidence_chain_flow: Problem → Evidence → Requirements → Constraints → Candidate Interventions → Evaluation → Best-Fit Approach — not: AI → Find Somewhere to Use It.

explicit_assumptions.title: Explicit Assumptions
explicit_assumptions.body: Assumptions are identified rather than presented as facts.

traceable_evidence.title: Traceable Evidence
traceable_evidence.body: Important conclusions should be connected to the evidence supporting them.

alternative_hypotheses.title: Alternative Hypotheses
alternative_hypotheses.body: Where uncertainty exists, competing explanations should be considered.

measurable_outcomes.title: Measurable Outcomes
measurable_outcomes.body: Success criteria are defined before implementation where practicable.

proportionate_rigor.title: Proportionate Rigor
proportionate_rigor.body: The level of analysis should reflect the cost, complexity and risk of the decision.

research_discovery_page.artifacts_title: Research That Leads to Engineering Decisions.
research_discovery_page.artifacts_p1: Research & Discovery is not intended to end with a presentation full of observations. It should produce artifacts that can inform an engineering decision. Depending on engagement scope, these may include:

research_findings_brief.title: Research & Findings Brief
research_findings_brief.body: The problem context, evidence, observations and principal findings.

stakeholder_objective_model.title: Stakeholder & Objective Model
stakeholder_objective_model.body: Who is affected, who owns decisions and which outcomes matter.

current_state_workflow_model.title: Current-State Workflow Model
current_state_workflow_model.body: How work and information move through the organization today.

systems_data_landscape.title: Systems & Data Landscape
systems_data_landscape.body: Applications, interfaces, data sources, dependencies and technical constraints.

root_cause_analysis.title: Root-Cause Analysis
root_cause_analysis.body: Evidence-supported explanations for the observed condition.

baseline_measurements.title: Baseline Measurements
baseline_measurements.body: Current performance against relevant operational or technical indicators.

requirements_definition.title: Requirements Definition
requirements_definition.body: Functional, technical, operational and governance requirements identified during discovery.

feasibility_assessment.title: Feasibility Assessment
feasibility_assessment.body: Technical, data, integration and operational feasibility where required.

opportunity_map.title: Opportunity Map
opportunity_map.body: Potential interventions prioritized according to evidence, value, feasibility and risk.

constraint_risk_register.title: Constraint & Risk Register
constraint_risk_register.body: Known limitations, assumptions, dependencies and material risks.

research_discovery_page.decision_gate_title: Research Ends With a Decision — Not a Sales Pitch.
research_discovery_page.decision_gate_p1: The purpose of discovery is not to guarantee that a project proceeds. It is to establish whether it should. A discovery engagement can therefore conclude with one of several directions:

proceed.title: Proceed
proceed.body: The problem is sufficiently defined, the evidence supports intervention and an engineering path appears feasible.

investigate_further.title: Investigate Further
investigate_further.body: Important uncertainty remains and additional evidence is required.

reframe.title: Reframe
reframe.body: The original problem or proposed intervention does not match what the investigation found.

redesign_approach.title: Redesign the Approach
redesign_approach.body: The objective remains valid, but a different technical or operational intervention is more appropriate.

do_not_build.title: Do Not Build
do_not_build.body: Expected value, feasibility or risk does not justify implementation.

research_discovery_page.decision_gate_p2_not_building: Not building the wrong system can be as valuable as building the right one.
research_discovery_page.transition_p1: Research & Discovery does not exist separately from the engineering lifecycle. Its outputs become inputs to the next stage: Evidence → Validated Problem Definition → Requirements → Constraints & Risks → Success Criteria → Strategy & Architecture.
research_discovery_page.transition_p2_should_emerge: Architecture should not begin as a collection of preferred technologies. It should emerge from a defensible understanding of what the system must accomplish, within which constraints, for which stakeholders, at what acceptable level of risk, and against which measurable outcomes.
research_discovery_page.step_02_description: Turn a validated problem into an engineered system direction.
research_discovery_page.start_p1: You do not need to arrive with an AI strategy. Bring the operational challenge, technical constraint, research question or business objective. We begin by determining what is actually happening — and what the evidence says should happen next.
research_discovery_page.references_intro: We reference these sources directly rather than hide them, because our methodology draws on established principles from scientific inquiry, systems engineering, requirements engineering, business analysis and risk management.

bcg_2024.title: Boston Consulting Group — Where's the Value in AI? (2024)
bcg_2024.body: Based on a survey of 1,000 CxOs and senior executives across more than 20 sectors and 59 countries; the source of the 74% / 26% figures and the 10–20–70 principle referenced above.

mckinsey_2025.title: McKinsey & Company — The State of AI: Global Survey 2025
mckinsey_2025.body: Source of the scaling and enterprise-level EBIT impact data, and of the finding on the importance of workflow redesign among higher-performing organizations.

iso_15288.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 — Systems and Software Engineering — System Life Cycle Processes
iso_15288.body: The primary engineering reference for treating systems, their elements, lifecycle and stakeholders in a structured way.

iso_29148.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 — Requirements Engineering
iso_29148.body: Specifies processes and information items for requirements engineering across systems and software lifecycles; ISO confirmed the edition as current following a 2024 review.

nist_ai_rmf.title: NIST — Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
nist_ai_rmf.body: Supports contextual AI risk thinking through Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, with continuous risk management across the AI lifecycle. NIST's AI RMF 1.0 is under active revision, which is why we name the version explicitly rather than imply it is always the latest final release.

strategy_architecture_page.eyebrow: Strategy & Architecture · Step 02 · How We Work
strategy_architecture_page.title: From Validated Problem to Engineered Direction.
strategy_architecture_page.intro_p1: Strategy and architecture do not begin as a collection of preferred technologies. They emerge from a defensible understanding of what the system must accomplish, within which constraints, for which stakeholders, and against which measurable outcomes.
strategy_architecture_page.intro_p2: This stage turns the outputs of Research & Discovery into an engineered system direction — the requirements, constraints and success criteria become architecture decisions, not the other way around.
strategy_architecture_page.hero_tags: Strategy · Architecture · Data Design · Security by Design · Technology Selection
strategy_architecture_page.bridge_p1: Every input to this stage was produced during Research & Discovery — not assumed, and not invented to justify a preferred technology.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.body: Functional, technical, operational and governance requirements identified during discovery.

constraints_risks.title: Constraints & Risks
constraints_risks.body: Technical, budget, regulatory and organizational constraints, alongside known risks and assumptions.

success_criteria.title: Success Criteria
success_criteria.body: Baselines, targets and the measurable evidence that would constitute improvement.

strategy_architecture_page.bridge_p2_not_from_scratch: Architecture decisions are traceable back to a validated problem definition — not to a preference for a particular vendor or framework.
strategy_architecture_page.strategy_vs_arch_title: Two Different Questions, Answered in Order.
strategy_architecture_page.strategy_vs_arch_p1: Strategy and architecture are often used interchangeably, but they answer different questions. Strategy asks what direction the business should take. Architecture asks how that direction gets built.

strategy_card.title: Strategy
strategy_card.body: Business objectives and a transformation roadmap — the direction the organization needs to move in, and why.

architecture_card.title: Architecture
architecture_card.body: Intelligent, scalable, secure and future-ready — the engineered structure that turns that direction into a system that can actually be built and operated.

strategy_architecture_page.principles_title: The Principles That Govern Every Decision.
strategy_architecture_page.principles_p1: Every architecture decision at OpenQCore is evaluated against the same set of principles, regardless of industry or engagement.

scalability.title: Scalability
scalability.body: The system should grow with demand without requiring a redesign at each stage of growth.

security_by_design.title: Security by Design
security_by_design.body: Security controls are built into the architecture from the start, not layered on afterward.

modularity.title: Modularity
modularity.body: Components can be replaced, upgraded or extended independently of one another.

interoperability.title: Interoperability
interoperability.body: The architecture connects cleanly with existing and future external systems.

observability.title: Observability
observability.body: The system's behavior, performance and failures can be seen and understood in operation.

cost_efficiency.title: Cost-Efficiency
cost_efficiency.body: Architecture decisions account for total operating cost, not just initial build cost.

future_readiness.title: Future-Readiness
future_readiness.body: The architecture can absorb changing requirements without a full rebuild.

strategy_architecture_page.inputs_p1: Requirements, constraints and risks, and success criteria from the discovery stage converge into specific architecture decisions — which then compose into a reference architecture for the engagement.
strategy_architecture_page.reference_arch_title: A Structure Built in Layers, Not Assumptions.
strategy_architecture_page.reference_arch_p1: OpenQCore's reference architecture separates concerns into distinct layers — interfaces, the intelligence and application layer, the data layer, and the underlying infrastructure — with security, governance, observability and scalability treated as cross-cutting concerns rather than afterthoughts.
strategy_architecture_page.governance_by_design_p1: Data strategy, security and compliance requirements are designed into the architecture from the beginning — not retrofitted once a system is already built.
strategy_architecture_page.governance_by_design_p2_not_afterthought: A system that requires governance to be added later is a system that was not architected correctly the first time.
strategy_architecture_page.tech_selection_title: Technology Follows the Requirements, Not the Other Way Around.
strategy_architecture_page.tech_selection_p1: OpenQCore evaluates candidate technologies against explicit criteria rather than defaulting to what is popular or familiar.

fit_for_purpose.title: Fit-for-Purpose
fit_for_purpose.body: Does the technology actually solve the problem defined during discovery?

total_cost_of_ownership.title: Total Cost of Ownership
total_cost_of_ownership.body: What does the technology cost to run, maintain and scale over time, not just to adopt?

vendor_lock_in_risk.title: Vendor Lock-In Risk
vendor_lock_in_risk.body: How difficult would it be to migrate away from this technology later?

team_capability.title: Team Capability
team_capability.body: Can the technology be operated and maintained by the teams who will own it?

long_term_maintainability.title: Long-Term Maintainability
long_term_maintainability.body: Will the technology remain supportable and upgradable over the system's expected lifetime?

strategy_architecture_page.tech_selection_p2_evidence_echo: As in discovery, the answer is not automatically predetermined — the evidence and requirements decide which technology, if any, is appropriate.
strategy_architecture_page.adr_title: Every Decision Is Documented, Not Assumed.
strategy_architecture_page.adr_p1: Architecture decisions involve trade-offs. OpenQCore records the reasoning behind significant decisions as Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), so the rationale remains visible long after the decision is made.
strategy_architecture_page.adr_p2_documented: A documented trade-off can be revisited as conditions change. An undocumented one is simply forgotten.

reference_architecture_document.title: Reference Architecture Document
reference_architecture_document.body: The layered architecture, its components and how they connect.

technology_stack_decision.title: Technology Stack Decision
technology_stack_decision.body: The selected technologies and the evaluation behind each choice.

data_architecture_blueprint.title: Data Architecture Blueprint
data_architecture_blueprint.body: How data is structured, stored, secured and made accessible across the system.

security_compliance_model.title: Security & Compliance Model
security_compliance_model.body: The security controls and compliance posture built into the architecture.

scalability_capacity_plan.title: Scalability & Capacity Plan
scalability_capacity_plan.body: How the system is expected to grow, and what that growth requires.

architecture_decision_records.title: Architecture Decision Records
architecture_decision_records.body: The documented rationale, trade-offs and consequences behind key decisions.

strategy_architecture_page.transition_title: A Direction, Not Yet a Build.
strategy_architecture_page.transition_p1: Strategy & Architecture defines how the system should be structured. The next stage turns that structure into a concrete solution design — the specific systems, workflows and interfaces to be built.
strategy_architecture_page.step_03_description: Turn an engineered direction into a specific, buildable solution.

solution_design_page.eyebrow: Solution Design · Step 03 · How We Work
solution_design_page.title: A Specification Is Not a Guess.
solution_design_page.intro_p1: Strategy & Architecture defines how a system should be structured. Solution Design determines exactly what gets built — the specific workflows, interfaces, data contracts and failure behaviors that turn an engineered direction into something a team can actually construct.
solution_design_page.intro_p2: This stage does not begin with an implementation. It begins with a specification that has been tested against evidence before a single line of production code is written.
solution_design_page.intro_should_be: "Does this specific design actually behave the way we expect, under the conditions it will really face — and can we prove that before committing engineering effort to build it?"
solution_design_page.bridge_title: A Structure Is Not Yet a System.
solution_design_page.bridge_p1: The reference architecture from the previous stage defines layers, technology choices and cross-cutting concerns. It does not yet define how a specific workflow should behave when a request is ambiguous, or what happens when an integration returns malformed data. Solution Design closes that gap — without it, "architecture" remains a diagram, not a system.
solution_design_page.rigor_title: The Cost of a Mistake Grows With Every Stage It Survives.
solution_design_page.rigor_p1: Barry Boehm's research into software engineering economics — first published in 1976 and expanded in his 1981 book Software Engineering Economics — found that the cost of correcting a defect grows substantially the later it is discovered.
solution_design_page.stat_design_label: Cost to fix a defect caught during design.
solution_design_page.stat_production_label: Cost to fix the same defect after production release, depending on project scale.
solution_design_page.stat_boehm_source: Boehm, Software Engineering Economics (1981); Boehm & Basili, IEEE Computer (2001).
solution_design_page.rigor_p2_revisited: This finding has been revisited since. Boehm and Basili's own 2001 revision found the curve is meaningfully flatter for smaller, fast-iterating teams with strong testing and continuous delivery. The multiplier is not universal, and we do not treat it as one.
solution_design_page.rigor_p3_direction_holds: But the direction of the finding has not been overturned: catching a design flaw before it is built is cheaper than catching it after. This is why OpenQCore treats prototyping and testing as part of design itself — not as a phase that happens once building has already started.
solution_design_page.specification_title: Turning Layers Into Decisions a Team Can Build From.
solution_design_page.specification_p1: Every architectural decision from the previous stage gets decomposed into concrete specifications.

workflow_specification.title: Workflow Specification
workflow_specification.body: The exact sequence of steps, decision points, exceptions and handoffs a solution must support — grounded in the Current-State Workflow Model produced during discovery, not a reimagined ideal process.

interface_specification.title: Interface Specification
interface_specification.body: What each user, system or agent actually sees, sends and receives — screens, conversational flows, API contracts, and the fields that matter at each step.

data_contract_specification.title: Data Contract Specification
data_contract_specification.body: The exact shape, validation rules, versioning approach and ownership of data moving between components.

behavioral_specification.title: Behavioral Specification
behavioral_specification.body: What the system does — and explicitly does not do — under normal conditions, edge cases, and failure conditions.

solution_design_page.workflow_title: Design the Work, Not Just the Interface.
solution_design_page.workflow_p1: A conversational interface layered on top of a broken workflow does not fix the workflow — it hides it, until the underlying constraint resurfaces somewhere else.
solution_design_page.workflow_p2: Solution Design starts from the workflow evidence gathered during discovery, and asks a structural question before an interface question: which steps in this process should be automated, which should remain human, and where exactly does responsibility hand off between them? We map this explicitly, so that human-in-the-loop points are a deliberate design decision — not an accident of what the technology happened to be capable of.

human_in_the_loop_points.title: Human-in-the-Loop Points
human_in_the_loop_points.body: Explicit checkpoints where human review, judgment or authorization is required by design — not by omission.

automation_boundaries.title: Automation Boundaries
automation_boundaries.body: Precisely defined limits on what a system is permitted to decide or execute without human sign-off.

exception_pathways.title: Exception Pathways
exception_pathways.body: Designed routes for cases that fall outside normal handling — not silent failures or default fallbacks.

solution_design_page.prototyping_title: Design as a Testable Hypothesis, Not a Finished Answer.
solution_design_page.prototyping_p1: OpenQCore treats early-stage design the way design science treats an information systems artifact: as something built specifically so it can be evaluated against a real problem, not simply admired for its elegance. This approach — formalized in Hevner et al.'s influential Design Science in Information Systems Research (MIS Quarterly, 2004) — treats the artifact and its evaluation as inseparable. We apply the same hypothesis-driven reasoning used during discovery, at the design level.

design.title: Design
design.body: A specific, falsifiable design decision — not a vague direction.

prototype.title: Prototype
prototype.body: A working representation sufficient to test the decision — not necessarily production-grade.

test_representative_data.title: Test With Representative Data
test_representative_data.body: Real or realistically representative inputs, not idealized examples chosen to succeed.

measure_baseline.title: Measure Against Baseline
measure_baseline.body: Comparison against the baseline and success criteria established during discovery — not a subjective impression of quality.

refine_or_reject.title: Refine or Reject
refine_or_reject.body: The design is kept, modified or abandoned based on what the test showed — not based on how much work has already gone into it.

solution_design_page.prototyping_p2_objective: The objective of a prototype is not to demonstrate that a design can work. It is to determine whether it reliably does, under the conditions the finished system will actually face.
solution_design_page.data_interface_p1: Integration failures rarely originate from a single obviously wrong decision. They tend to originate from ambiguity — a field that was assumed to always be present, an error case nobody wrote down, a version mismatch nobody planned for.
solution_design_page.data_interface_p2_unglamorous: This is deliberately unglamorous work. It is also the work that determines whether a system that performs well in a demo continues to perform well in production, six integrations and eighteen months later.
solution_design_page.failure_label: Designing for Failure, Not Just Success
solution_design_page.failure_title: Every Demo Succeeds. Not Every System Does.
solution_design_page.failure_p1: Most design failures are not failures of the happy path. They are failures of what happens when something goes wrong — an upstream system times out, a document doesn't extract cleanly, a model is uncertain, a user does something unexpected. OpenQCore designs these conditions deliberately rather than discovering them in production.

uncertainty_handling.title: Uncertainty Handling
uncertainty_handling.body: What the system does when confidence in an output is low — including whether and how it says so.

graceful_degradation.title: Graceful Degradation
graceful_degradation.body: What functions remain available when a dependency fails, rather than a full-system outage.

escalation_design.title: Escalation Design
escalation_design.body: The specific conditions under which a case is handed to a human, and what context that handoff carries with it.

adversarial_edge_case_behavior.title: Adversarial & Edge-Case Behavior
adversarial_edge_case_behavior.body: How the system behaves under malformed input, unexpected sequences, or attempted misuse — not just well-formed requests.

solution_design_page.failure_p2_not_designed: A system that has never been asked "what happens when this fails?" has not really been designed. It has only been demonstrated.
solution_design_page.validation_title: Acceptance Criteria Come Before the Code, Not After.
solution_design_page.validation_p1: Consistent with the principle established during discovery — that success must be defined before implementation — Solution Design produces explicit, written acceptance criteria and a test plan before production development begins.

functional_acceptance.title: Functional Acceptance Criteria
functional_acceptance.body: What the solution must correctly do, stated in testable terms.

non_functional_acceptance.title: Non-Functional Acceptance Criteria
non_functional_acceptance.body: Consistent with recognized software quality characteristics — including performance efficiency, reliability, usability, security and maintainability, as organized by ISO/IEC 25010's software product quality model — specified as measurable targets rather than general aspirations.

test_plan.title: Test Plan
test_plan.body: The specific scenarios, data sets and conditions the solution will be evaluated against before it is considered ready to build in production form.

solution_design_page.gate_title: Design Ends With a Decision — Not an Automatic Green Light.
solution_design_page.gate_p1: This practice has precedent: Michael Fagan's formal design and code inspection method, introduced at IBM in 1976, established that structured, criteria-based review catches defects earlier and more reliably than informal approval. OpenQCore applies the same principle to solution design.

proceed_to_build.title: Proceed to Build
proceed_to_build.body: The specification is sufficiently precise, the prototype met its evaluation criteria, and development can begin.

iterate_design.title: Iterate Design
iterate_design.body: The core direction is sound, but specific elements need revision based on what testing revealed.

return_to_architecture.title: Return to Architecture
return_to_architecture.body: Design work revealed a constraint the architecture did not account for — the appropriate response is revising the structure, not designing around it.

escalate_risk.title: Escalate Risk
escalate_risk.body: Design work surfaced a risk — technical, operational, security or ethical — that requires a decision above the design team's authority before proceeding.

solution_design_page.gate_p2_not_automatic: A design gate that always says yes is not a gate.
solution_design_page.artifacts_title: Specifications a Team Can Actually Build From.
solution_design_page.artifacts_p1: Depending on engagement scope, this stage produces:

solution_specification_document.title: Solution Specification Document
solution_specification_document.body: Workflows, interfaces, data contracts and behavior, in enough detail to build from without re-deriving intent.

interaction_workflow_diagrams.title: Interaction & Workflow Diagrams
interaction_workflow_diagrams.body: Visual representations of process flow, including explicit human-in-the-loop points.

api_data_contracts.title: API & Data Contracts
api_data_contracts.body: Schemas, validation rules and versioning strategy for every interface between components.

prototype_evaluation_report.title: Prototype Evaluation Report
prototype_evaluation_report.body: What was tested, against what baseline, and what the results support or rule out.

failure_mode_analysis.title: Failure Mode Analysis
failure_mode_analysis.body: Documented failure conditions and the designed system response to each.

acceptance_criteria_test_plan.title: Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan
acceptance_criteria_test_plan.body: The specific, measurable conditions the built solution must satisfy before deployment.

solution_design_page.transition_title: A Specification Is Not Yet Software.
solution_design_page.transition_p1: Solution Design produces a tested, validated specification — not a finished system. The next stage turns that specification into working software, integrated with the systems it must operate alongside.
solution_design_page.transition_flow: Solution Specification → Prototype Evaluation → Acceptance Criteria → Development & Integration
solution_design_page.step_04_description: Build the specified solution against defined acceptance criteria — not against assumption.

boehm_1981.title: Boehm, B. — Software Engineering Economics (1981); Boehm, B. & Basili, V. — "Software Defect Reduction Top 10 List," IEEE Computer (2001)
boehm_1981.body: Source of the cost-of-change findings referenced above, including the later revision showing a flatter curve for smaller, fast-iterating teams.

hevner_2004.title: Hevner, A., March, S., Park, J., & Ram, S. — "Design Science in Information Systems Research," MIS Quarterly (2004)
hevner_2004.body: Foundational framework for treating an information systems artifact and its evaluation as inseparable — the basis for the prototype-test-refine cycle described above.

fagan_1976.title: Fagan, M. — "Design and Code Inspections to Reduce Errors in Program Development," IBM Systems Journal (1976)
fagan_1976.body: Origin of structured, criteria-based design review as a formal engineering practice, referenced in the Design Review Gate above.

iso_25010.title: ISO/IEC 25010:2011 — Systems and Software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — System and Software Quality Models
iso_25010.body: Source of the non-functional quality characteristics referenced in the acceptance criteria above.

development_integration_page.eyebrow: Development & Integration · Step 04 · How We Work
development_integration_page.title: A Specification Becomes Software.
development_integration_page.intro_p1: Solution Design produces a tested specification and defined acceptance criteria. This stage turns that specification into working, verified software — integrated with the systems it must operate alongside, and proven against the criteria defined before development began.
development_integration_page.intro_p2: Development here is not interpretation. Every implementation decision traces back to a specification produced during design — not to what a developer assumed the intent probably was.
development_integration_page.intro_should_be: "Does the built system satisfy the acceptance criteria defined before we started — under real integration conditions, not just in isolation?"
development_integration_page.hero_tags: Implementation · Verification · Integration · Traceability · Delivery Discipline
development_integration_page.bridge_p1: Every input to this stage was produced during Solution Design: the Solution Specification Document, the Prototype Evaluation Report, and the Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan. Development against an untested specification would simply move the risk that prototyping was meant to retire back into production code.
development_integration_page.bridge_flow: Solution Specification + Acceptance Criteria → Verified Implementation
development_integration_page.discipline_title: Speed and Stability Are Measured Together, Not Traded Off.
development_integration_page.discipline_p1: Software delivery performance is not simply a matter of how fast a team writes code. Research by Forsgren, Humble and Kim — published in Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (2018), based on the DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) program's multi-year research across thousands of organizations — identified two categories of engineering performance that must be measured together: throughput and stability.
development_integration_page.stat_lead_time_label: How long it takes a validated change to move from commit to a deployable state.
development_integration_page.stat_change_failure_label: The percentage of changes that introduce a defect requiring remediation.
development_integration_page.stat_dora_source: Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate (2018); DORA, State of DevOps research.
development_integration_page.discipline_p2_balanced: A team that ships quickly but frequently breaks things is not performing well by this research — and neither is a team that ships safely but too slowly to matter. OpenQCore holds both dimensions in view during this stage, rather than optimizing for velocity alone.
development_integration_page.implementation_title: Every Line of Work Traces to a Requirement.
development_integration_page.implementation_p1: Implementation work is decomposed directly from the Solution Specification and Acceptance Criteria — not from a general understanding of what the design "was going for."

traceable_work_breakdown.title: Traceable Work Breakdown
traceable_work_breakdown.body: Each implementation task is linked to a specific requirement or acceptance criterion — not a loosely related feature description.

definition_of_done.title: Definition of Done
definition_of_done.body: A task is not complete when code is written. It is complete when it satisfies its linked acceptance criterion under test.

specification_drift_control.title: Specification Drift Control
specification_drift_control.body: Where implementation reveals a gap or ambiguity in the specification, the specification is updated and reviewed — not silently reinterpreted by whoever is writing the code that day.

development_integration_page.testing_title: Verification Happens at Every Layer, Not Just at the End.
development_integration_page.testing_p1: OpenQCore structures verification according to the testing pyramid — a widely used framework, popularized by Mike Cohn, for balancing test coverage across layers of a system rather than concentrating it in slow, expensive end-to-end tests.

unit_tests.title: Unit Tests
unit_tests.body: Fast, isolated verification of individual components against their specified behavior — including their behavior under invalid input.

integration_tests.title: Integration Tests
integration_tests.body: Verification that components correctly interact according to the data contracts defined during solution design.

end_to_end_tests.title: End-to-End Tests
end_to_end_tests.body: Verification of complete workflows against the acceptance criteria defined before development began — the smallest, most expensive layer, reserved for what genuinely requires it.

development_integration_page.testing_p2_objective: The objective is not maximum test count. It is confidence that the acceptance criteria are genuinely satisfied, at the lowest cost layer capable of proving it.
development_integration_page.contracts_title: An API Contract Is Only Real If It's Tested, Not Just Documented.
development_integration_page.contracts_p1: The data and API contracts specified during Solution Design are not treated as documentation to be followed informally. OpenQCore applies consumer-driven contract testing — an approach formalized in tools such as Pact — where each integration point is verified against an executable contract both sides of the integration must satisfy.
development_integration_page.contracts_p2: This matters specifically for systems that must connect to existing infrastructure: a contract that is only checked by manual review can drift silently as either side changes. A contract that is tested automatically cannot.
development_integration_page.review_title: A Second Reviewer Catches What the Author Cannot.
development_integration_page.review_p1: Widely cited research on peer code review — including the study conducted at Cisco Systems and popularized in Cohen et al.'s Best Kept Secrets of Peer Code Review — found that review effectiveness depends heavily on pace and scope: smaller, more frequent reviews conducted without time pressure catch substantially more defects than large reviews conducted quickly.
development_integration_page.review_p2: OpenQCore applies structured code review alongside automated static analysis — style, complexity, and known-vulnerability scanning — as a standing verification layer, not an optional courtesy pass before merge.
development_integration_page.pipeline_title: Every Change Is Verified the Same Way, Automatically.
development_integration_page.pipeline_p1: Commit → Automated Build → Unit & Integration Tests → Static & Security Analysis → Contract Verification → Ready for Deployment.
development_integration_page.pipeline_p2_note: Manual, inconsistent verification does not scale, and it does not produce a reliable signal about whether a change is actually safe to release — a determination made in the next stage, Deployment & Enablement. What this stage guarantees is that a change reaching that gate has already been verified against the same automated standard as every change before it.
development_integration_page.security_title: Security Is Verified During Development, Not Audited Afterward.
development_integration_page.security_p1: OpenQCore's development practices align with the structure described in NIST's Secure Software Development Framework (SP 800-218) — organizing security activity around preparing the organization, protecting software, producing well-secured software, and responding to vulnerabilities.

dependency_vulnerability_scanning.title: Dependency & Vulnerability Scanning
dependency_vulnerability_scanning.body: Automated scanning of third-party dependencies for known vulnerabilities as part of the standard pipeline, not a periodic manual audit.

threat_modeling.title: Threat Modeling
threat_modeling.body: Structured consideration of how a component could be misused, informed by the failure modes defined during solution design.

least_privilege_implementation.title: Least-Privilege Implementation
least_privilege_implementation.body: Access and permission scopes implemented at the narrowest level that satisfies the specification — not the broadest level that is convenient.

development_integration_page.gate_title: A Build Is Not Ready Because It Compiles.
development_integration_page.gate_p1: Every change reaches a defined verification gate before it can be considered for deployment.

ready_for_deployment.title: Ready for Deployment
ready_for_deployment.body: All acceptance criteria are met, verified through automated tests, contract checks and security scanning.

return_for_fixes.title: Return for Fixes
return_for_fixes.body: Specific, identified defects must be resolved before this change can proceed.

return_to_design.title: Return to Design
return_to_design.body: Implementation revealed that the specification itself does not hold under real conditions — the correct response is revising the specification, not coding around it.

escalate_risk.title: Escalate Risk
escalate_risk.body: A security, compliance or architectural risk was identified that requires a decision above the development team's authority.

development_integration_page.gate_p2_not_verifying: A pipeline that always reaches "ready for deployment" is not verifying anything.
development_integration_page.artifacts_title: Software Ready for the Decision to Deploy — Not Yet Deployed.
development_integration_page.artifacts_p1: Depending on engagement scope, this stage produces:

verified_codebase.title: Verified Codebase
verified_codebase.body: Implementation traceable to specification, passing all defined verification layers.

test_coverage_report.title: Test Coverage Report
test_coverage_report.body: Unit, integration and end-to-end test results mapped to acceptance criteria.

contract_test_suite.title: Contract Test Suite
contract_test_suite.body: Executable verification of every integration point defined during solution design.

code_review_records.title: Code Review Records
code_review_records.body: Documented review history and resolution of raised issues.

security_scan_results.title: Security Scan Results
security_scan_results.body: Dependency, vulnerability and static analysis findings and their resolution.

ci_pipeline_documentation.title: CI Pipeline Documentation
ci_pipeline_documentation.body: The automated verification pipeline applied to this change, and to every change after it.

development_integration_page.transition_title: Verified Software Is Not Yet Live Software.
development_integration_page.transition_p1: Development & Integration produces software that has been verified against its specification — not software that has been released, monitored, or proven stable under real production load. The next stage governs how, when and how safely that software actually reaches production.
development_integration_page.transition_flow: Solution Specification → Verified Implementation → Deployment & Enablement
development_integration_page.step_05_description: Release verified software into production safely, deliberately, and with a defined path to rollback.

accelerate_dora.body: Source of the delivery performance metrics referenced above.

cohn_testing_pyramid.title: Cohn, M. — Succeeding with Agile (2009)
cohn_testing_pyramid.body: Source of the testing pyramid concept referenced in test-driven verification above.

cohen_peer_review.title: Cohen, J. et al. — Best Kept Secrets of Peer Code Review (SmartBear, based on research at Cisco Systems)
cohen_peer_review.body: Source of the code review effectiveness findings referenced above.

pact_contracts.body: An established approach to executable, automatically verified integration contracts, referenced in the integration testing section above.

nist_ssdf.title: NIST — Secure Software Development Framework, SP 800-218
nist_ssdf.body: Source of the structure referenced in secure development practices above.

deployment_enablement_page.eyebrow: Deployment & Enablement · Step 05 · How We Work
deployment_enablement_page.title: Release Is a Decision, Not an Event.
deployment_enablement_page.intro_p1: Development & Integration produces verified software — but verified software is not yet live software. This stage governs how, when, and how safely that software is exposed to real production traffic, and ensures the people responsible for operating it are ready before it arrives.
deployment_enablement_page.intro_p2: Deployment at OpenQCore is treated as a controlled exposure of risk, not a single irreversible moment. A release is not "done" when code reaches production. It is done when it has been exposed gradually, observed under real conditions, and confirmed safe — with a defined path back if it is not.
deployment_enablement_page.intro_should_be: "How do we expose this change to real users in a way that limits the blast radius of anything we did not anticipate — and can we reverse it quickly if we need to?"
deployment_enablement_page.hero_tags: Progressive Delivery · Risk Containment · Reversibility · Readiness · Enablement
deployment_enablement_page.bridge_title: Verified Is Not the Same as Proven in Production.
deployment_enablement_page.bridge_p1: The previous stage confirms that a change satisfies its acceptance criteria under test. It does not confirm how that change behaves under real production load, real user behavior, or real interactions with systems that cannot be fully replicated in a test environment. Deployment & Enablement exists precisely because that gap is real — and because closing it safely requires its own discipline.
deployment_enablement_page.bridge_flow: Ready for Deployment → Controlled Production Exposure
deployment_enablement_page.discipline_title: Speed Without Reversibility Is Not Progress.
deployment_enablement_page.discipline_p1: The same DORA research introduced during Development & Integration — Forsgren, Humble and Kim's Accelerate (2018) — pairs its throughput metrics with two stability metrics that matter specifically at this stage.
deployment_enablement_page.stat_frequency_label: How often an organization successfully releases to production.
deployment_enablement_page.stat_restore_label: How long it takes to recover when a deployment degrades production.
deployment_enablement_page.stat_dora_source: Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate (2018); DORA, State of DevOps research.
deployment_enablement_page.discipline_p2_single_objective: High-performing organizations, in this research, do not simply deploy often — they deploy in a way that keeps recovery time short when something goes wrong. OpenQCore treats these as a single objective, not a trade-off: the practices in this stage are designed to make deployment both frequent and quickly reversible.
deployment_enablement_page.strategies_title: Separate the Decision to Release From the Decision to Deploy.
deployment_enablement_page.strategies_p1: Practices formalized in Humble and Farley's influential Continuous Delivery (2010) distinguish deploying a change from releasing it to users — a distinction OpenQCore treats as a foundational design choice for how software reaches production.

blue_green.title: Blue-Green Deployment
blue_green.body: Two complete production environments, with traffic switched from one to the other — allowing an instant, full reversal if the new environment misbehaves.

canary_releases.title: Canary Releases
canary_releases.body: A new version is exposed to a small fraction of real traffic first, observed against defined signals, and only expanded once those signals hold.

feature_flags.title: Feature Flags
feature_flags.body: Code can be deployed to production while remaining inactive for users — separating the act of shipping code from the act of exposing a capability.

deployment_enablement_page.environments_title: A Change Earns Its Way to Production. It Is Not Sent There Directly.
deployment_enablement_page.environments_p1: A change moves through defined environments — development, staging, and production — with explicit verification at each promotion, not a single test pass followed by a direct release.

development.title: Development
development.body: Where a change is built and initially verified in isolation.

staging.title: Staging
staging.body: Where a change is verified against production-like conditions, configuration, and integrations.

production.title: Production
production.body: Where a change is exposed to real traffic — progressively, and under observation.

deployment_enablement_page.rollback_title: The Rollback Plan Is Written Before the Deployment, Not During the Incident.
deployment_enablement_page.rollback_p1: A rollback strategy decided while a system is already degraded is a rollback strategy decided under pressure, with incomplete information, and often too late. OpenQCore defines the rollback path for a change before it is deployed — not after something goes wrong.

rollback_trigger_conditions.title: Defined Rollback Trigger Conditions
rollback_trigger_conditions.body: The specific signals that would trigger a rollback, agreed in advance rather than judged in the moment.

data_state_compatibility.title: Data & State Compatibility
data_state_compatibility.body: Explicit consideration of whether a rollback is safe given any data or schema changes the deployment introduced.

recovery_time_objective.title: Recovery Time Objective
recovery_time_objective.body: A stated target for how quickly service should be restored if a rollback is required.

deployment_enablement_page.iac_title: A Deployment That Cannot Be Repeated Exactly Cannot Be Trusted.
deployment_enablement_page.iac_p1: Deployment steps are defined as code — version-controlled, reviewed, and executed identically every time — rather than performed as manual actions dependent on an individual's memory of the correct sequence. This is a foundational practice in the same body of continuous delivery research referenced above: a deployment process that cannot be reproduced exactly cannot be verified, and cannot be safely automated.
deployment_enablement_page.risk_title: Every Deployment Is Evaluated Before It Happens, Not After.
deployment_enablement_page.risk_p1: Consistent with the threat modeling introduced during Development & Integration, each deployment is assessed for its specific risk profile before it proceeds.

blast_radius.title: Blast Radius
blast_radius.body: How many users, systems, or workflows would be affected if this specific change behaves unexpectedly.

reversibility.title: Reversibility
reversibility.body: How quickly and cleanly this specific change can be undone if required.

dependency_exposure.title: Dependency Exposure
dependency_exposure.body: Which downstream systems or teams are affected by this deployment, and whether they have been informed.

deployment_enablement_page.rollout_title: Exposure Increases Only When the Evidence Supports It.
deployment_enablement_page.rollout_p1: Canary (small percentage) → Monitor defined signals → Expand exposure → Monitor defined signals → Full rollout. At any point in this sequence, a rollback is a designed outcome — not an emergency improvisation. Expansion to the next stage is a decision made against evidence gathered at the current stage, not a default that happens automatically with time.
deployment_enablement_page.rollout_p2_error_budget: This approach reflects the concept of an error budget, described in Google's Site Reliability Engineering (2016): a defined, acceptable amount of instability that a system is permitted to spend, used to make the trade-off between release velocity and reliability an explicit, measured decision rather than an implicit one.
deployment_enablement_page.enablement_title: A System Nobody Can Operate Has Not Really Been Deployed.
deployment_enablement_page.enablement_p1: Deployment is frequently treated as complete once software runs in production. OpenQCore treats it as complete only once the people responsible for operating, supporting, and troubleshooting that software are actually prepared to do so.

operational_runbooks.title: Operational Runbooks
operational_runbooks.body: Documented procedures for common operational tasks, known failure modes, and how to respond to them.

on_call_readiness.title: On-Call Readiness
on_call_readiness.body: Confirmation that the people responsible for responding to incidents have the access, context, and escalation paths they need.

knowledge_transfer.title: Knowledge Transfer
knowledge_transfer.body: Explicit handoff of operational understanding to the team or organization who will own the system going forward.

deployment_enablement_page.gate_title: A Deployment Proceeds Because Evidence Supports It — Not Because It Is Scheduled.
deployment_enablement_page.gate_p1: Every planned deployment reaches a defined decision gate before it proceeds.

deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.body: Risk assessment, rollback plan, and readiness are all satisfied — the deployment proceeds.

delay.title: Delay
delay.body: An identified risk has not yet been sufficiently mitigated — the deployment waits until it has been.

rollback.title: Rollback
rollback.body: A deployed change has triggered a defined rollback condition — the previous state is restored.

escalate_incident.title: Escalate Incident
escalate_incident.body: A deployment has caused an impact requiring a formal incident response beyond a standard rollback.

deployment_enablement_page.gate_p2_not_a_schedule: A deployment gate that never delays or rolls back is not evaluating risk — it is simply recording a schedule.
deployment_enablement_page.artifacts_title: A Live System, and the Capability to Operate It.
deployment_enablement_page.artifacts_p1: Depending on engagement scope, this stage produces:

deployment_runbook.title: Deployment Runbook
deployment_runbook.body: The specific, repeatable procedure used to deploy this change and future changes like it.

rollback_plan.title: Rollback Plan
rollback_plan.body: The defined trigger conditions, procedure, and recovery time objective for reversing this deployment.

environment_promotion_record.title: Environment Promotion Record
environment_promotion_record.body: Documentation of how the change moved through development, staging, and production, and what was verified at each stage.

risk_assessment_document.title: Risk Assessment Document
risk_assessment_document.body: The blast radius, reversibility, and dependency exposure evaluated before deployment.

team_enablement_materials.title: Team Enablement Materials
team_enablement_materials.body: Runbooks, on-call readiness confirmation, and the knowledge transfer completed before handover.

progressive_rollout_report.title: Progressive Rollout Report
progressive_rollout_report.body: The signals observed at each stage of exposure, and the evidence supporting expansion to full rollout.

deployment_enablement_page.transition_title: Live Is Not the Same as Understood.
deployment_enablement_page.transition_p1: Deployment & Enablement produces a system that is running safely in production, with the people responsible for it prepared to operate it. It does not yet produce a continuous understanding of how that system behaves over time, or a structured mechanism for improving it. That is the purpose of the next and final stage in this methodology.
deployment_enablement_page.transition_flow: Controlled Production Exposure → Operational Readiness → Monitoring & Optimization
deployment_enablement_page.step_06_description: Understand how a live system actually behaves, and improve it continuously against real evidence.

accelerate_dora.body: Source of the deployment frequency and recovery time metrics referenced above.

continuous_delivery.body: Source of the deploy/release distinction, blue-green deployment, and infrastructure-as-code principles referenced above.
