sre_book.body: Source of the error budget concept referenced in the progressive rollout section above.

monitoring_optimization_page.eyebrow: Monitoring & Optimization · Step 06 · Final Stage · How We Work
monitoring_optimization_page.title: Live Software Is Not Finished Software.
monitoring_optimization_page.intro_p1: A system is not understood because it is running. It is understood because it is observed, measured, and continuously improved against evidence. This final stage closes the loop of the OpenQCore methodology — the evidence it produces becomes the starting point for the next question worth investigating.
monitoring_optimization_page.intro_should_be: "Do we actually understand how this system behaves under real conditions over time — and is that understanding driving continuous improvement, or simply confirming that nothing has crashed?"
monitoring_optimization_page.hero_tags: Observability · Incident Response · Continuous Improvement · Evidence · Feedback
monitoring_optimization_page.bridge_title: Operational Readiness Is a Starting Point, Not an End State.
monitoring_optimization_page.bridge_p1: Deployment & Enablement confirms that a system is running safely and that the people responsible for it are prepared. It does not yet produce a continuous, evidence-based understanding of how that system behaves as real usage, real data, and real conditions accumulate over time. That understanding is the purpose of this stage.
monitoring_optimization_page.discipline_title: Four Signals Indicate Whether a System Is Actually Healthy.
monitoring_optimization_page.discipline_p1: Google's Site Reliability Engineering (2016) — the same body of research referenced in the previous stage — identifies four signals considered sufficient, if monitored well, to understand the health of most systems: the golden signals.

latency.title: Latency
latency.body: The time it takes to service a request — distinguishing successful responses from failed ones.

traffic.title: Traffic
traffic.body: The demand being placed on the system, measured in terms relevant to its function.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: The rate of requests that fail, whether explicitly or through incorrect results.

saturation.title: Saturation
saturation.body: How close the system is to its resource limits, and how much headroom remains.

monitoring_optimization_page.discipline_source: Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering (2016).
monitoring_optimization_page.pillars_title: Data Is Not the Same as Understanding.
monitoring_optimization_page.pillars_p1: OpenQCore structures observability around three complementary data types — a framework widely used across the industry and formalized in the OpenTelemetry project (a CNCF-hosted open standard) and in Cindy Sridharan's Distributed Systems Observability (2018).

logs.title: Logs
logs.body: Discrete, timestamped records of individual events — the most granular signal, useful for reconstructing exactly what happened.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.body: Aggregated, numerical measurements over time — efficient for detecting trends and triggering alerts.

traces.title: Traces
traces.body: The path a single request takes across distributed components — essential for understanding where time and failures occur in complex systems.

monitoring_optimization_page.signals_title: Raw Data Has No Value Until It Is Interpreted.
monitoring_optimization_page.signals_p1: Logs, metrics and traces are not, by themselves, insight. They become useful once they are organized into dashboards that reveal patterns, alerts that surface what requires attention, and ultimately an understanding that can inform a decision.
monitoring_optimization_page.alerting_title: An Alert Nobody Trusts Is an Alert Nobody Reads.
monitoring_optimization_page.alerting_p1: A well-documented failure mode in operations teams — often called alert fatigue — occurs when alerting is based on any deviation from a number rather than on genuine impact to users or the system. The result is a high volume of alerts that are eventually ignored, including the ones that matter.

symptom_based_alerting.title: Symptom-Based Alerting
symptom_based_alerting.body: Alerts are triggered by observable impact — a user-facing symptom — rather than by any internal metric moving outside a range.

actionable_thresholds.title: Actionable Thresholds
actionable_thresholds.body: An alert exists only if there is a specific, defined action someone should take in response to it.

alert_review_cadence.title: Alert Review Cadence
alert_review_cadence.body: Alert rules are reviewed on a regular basis and retired when they no longer indicate a real, actionable condition.

monitoring_optimization_page.incident_title: Understand the System, Not Assign Blame.
monitoring_optimization_page.incident_p1: When an incident occurs, OpenQCore's response follows a documented, blameless postmortem practice — a concept formalized in Google's Site Reliability Engineering (2016) — in which the analysis focuses on the systemic conditions that allowed a failure to happen, not on the individual who happened to be involved.
monitoring_optimization_page.incident_p2: This distinction matters practically: teams that fear blame tend to under-report and obscure the conditions that caused a failure, which makes the same failure more likely to recur. A blameless process is designed to surface those conditions honestly, precisely because doing so is how they get fixed.
monitoring_optimization_page.feedback_loop_title: Monitoring Does Not End the Methodology. It Restarts It.
monitoring_optimization_page.feedback_loop_p1: The signals gathered during monitoring — performance trends, recurring incidents, model drift, unexpected usage patterns — are not simply reported and archived. They become evidence that can justify revisiting a problem definition, questioning an architectural assumption, or identifying an entirely new problem worth investigating.
monitoring_optimization_page.feedback_loop_p2_closes: This is what closes OpenQCore's six-stage methodology into a cycle rather than a straight line: evidence produced in Monitoring & Optimization flows back into Research & Discovery, where the process begins again on stronger footing than before.
monitoring_optimization_page.performance_title: Improvement Is Measured Against the Same Baseline That Defined Success.
monitoring_optimization_page.performance_p1: Optimization work is evaluated against the baseline and success criteria established during Research & Discovery — not against a general sense that a system has gotten better.

baseline_comparison.title: Baseline Comparison
baseline_comparison.body: Current performance is measured directly against the baseline recorded before the system existed in its current form.

regression_detection.title: Regression Detection
regression_detection.body: Changes that degrade a previously stable metric are identified and investigated, not absorbed as a new normal.

capacity_trend_analysis.title: Capacity Trend Analysis
capacity_trend_analysis.body: Resource usage trends are tracked to anticipate scaling needs before they become an incident.

monitoring_optimization_page.ai_monitoring_title: AI Systems Require Evidence That Traditional Monitoring Does Not Capture.
monitoring_optimization_page.ai_monitoring_p1: Consistent with the contextual risk analysis introduced during Research & Discovery, AI-specific components are monitored for signals that conventional application monitoring does not surface on its own.

model_drift_detection.title: Model Drift Detection
model_drift_detection.body: Ongoing measurement of whether a model's performance degrades as real-world data diverges from what it was built and evaluated against.

human_override_rate.title: Human Override Rate
human_override_rate.body: How often a human reviewer overrides an AI-generated recommendation or decision — a direct signal of where confidence in the system is, and is not, warranted.

evaluation_recalibration.title: Evaluation Recalibration
evaluation_recalibration.body: Periodic re-evaluation against updated evidence, rather than relying indefinitely on the evaluation completed before deployment.

monitoring_optimization_page.gate_title: Monitoring Concludes With a Decision, Not Just a Dashboard.
monitoring_optimization_page.gate_p1: Evidence gathered during monitoring is periodically reviewed against a defined decision gate.

continue_monitoring.title: Continue Monitoring
continue_monitoring.body: The system is performing within expected parameters — observation continues without a change in course.

optimize.title: Optimize
optimize.body: A specific, bounded improvement is justified by the evidence and can be pursued without revisiting the underlying problem definition.

re_enter_discovery.title: Re-Enter Discovery
re_enter_discovery.body: The evidence points to a problem broader than an optimization — the appropriate response is returning to Research & Discovery with what has been learned.

deprecate.title: Deprecate
deprecate.body: The evidence indicates the system no longer justifies its operating cost relative to the value it delivers.

monitoring_optimization_page.artifacts_title: Continuous Evidence, Not a One-Time Report.
monitoring_optimization_page.artifacts_p1: Depending on engagement scope, this stage produces:

observability_dashboard.title: Observability Dashboard
observability_dashboard.body: Live visualization of logs, metrics, and traces relevant to the system's health and the golden signals.

incident_response_runbook.title: Incident Response Runbook
incident_response_runbook.body: Documented procedures for responding to and resolving operational incidents.

postmortem_records.title: Postmortem Records
postmortem_records.body: Blameless analysis of incidents, their systemic causes, and the changes made in response.

performance_trend_report.title: Performance Trend Report
performance_trend_report.body: Performance measured over time against the original baseline and success criteria.

model_drift_report.title: Model Drift Report
model_drift_report.body: Tracked model performance against evolving real-world data and usage patterns.

optimization_backlog.title: Optimization Backlog
optimization_backlog.body: Evidence-justified improvement opportunities, prioritized for future work.

monitoring_optimization_page.closes_loop_p1: OpenQCore's six stages — Research & Discovery, Strategy & Architecture, Solution Design, Development & Integration, Deployment & Enablement, and Monitoring & Optimization — do not form a straight line that ends here. The evidence this stage produces becomes the starting point for the next problem worth investigating, whether that means refining the current system or identifying an entirely new one.
